details: @ubedsockets/baileys is a modified fork of the @whiskeysockets/baileys WhatsApp Web library that silently manipulates the account of whoever installs and connects it. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js the package stores a WhatsApp newsletter JID as a base64 string in an unreadably named constant (VzVzVzVzVzVzVzVzVzVzVzVzVz = "MTIwMzYzNDIzMTcwNDI0ODI4QG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI=", decoding to 120363423170424828@newsletter). Inside makeNewsletterSocket it schedules setTimeout(..., 90000) that decodes this constant and issues the WhatsApp FOLLOW query (query_id 7871414976211147) against it, wrapped in an empty catch block. The result: the user's linked WhatsApp account is enrolled into the operator's channel 90 seconds after a socket is created, with no API call from the integrator and no way to opt out. The same file hardcodes AUTO_REACT_NEWSLETTER = true and, on every newsletter message query, sends a 👍 reaction (query to the source newsletter JID) without being asked. package.json's homepage points at the operator's WhatsApp contact link (wa[.]me/6285147777105). lib/Socket/setup.js additionally forges forwarded-newsletter attribution on messages it sends: outgoing album and event messages carry forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo with newsletterJid 120363423295236859@newsletter, newsletterName "vezyn"/"veyzen", senderName "vyzen", forwardingScore 99999, isForwarded true, plus fabricated starred/label/disappearing-mode fields — making operator traffic look like it came from a branded channel. No install lifecycle hook is present; the manipulation happens at require/connect time inside the library's socket layer. IOC: WhatsApp channel 120363423170424828@newsletter (silent follow target).
